title: AI-driven peptide discovery for endometrial cancer: deep generative modeling and molecular simulation in the big data era.
authors: Fatima, Israr; Rehman, Abdur; Wang, Zhibo; Ur Rehman, Hafeez; Aldaw, Mohamed; Warraich, Dawood Ahmed; Meng, Yuxuan; Li, Yan; Liao, Mingzhi
one_liner_zh: 该文用AI生成与分子模拟设计靶向子宫内膜癌蛋白的肽类抑制剂，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接与MD，但对象为蛋白-小分子/肽，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联甚微。
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with molecular modeling offers new opportunities to accelerate therapeutic discovery. In this study, we developed an AI-driven generative pipeline combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and variational autoencoders (VAEs) to design novel peptide-like molecules targeting major proteins implicated in endometrial cancer (EC), including AKT1, ESR1, Connexin-43, and CTNNB1. From over 14,200 generated structures, approximately 2313 peptides met drug-likeness and structural criteria and were screened using deep learning-enhanced docking. Top-ranked peptides, such as Gitoxoside (- 11.53 kcal/mol) and 9-Fluoro-11 (- 11.38 kcal/mol), demonstrated stronger binding to AKT1 than the reference inhibitor Capivasertib (- 8.50 kcal/mol). Similar high-affinity interactions were observed for CTNNB1-SCHEMBL (- 12.33 kcal/mol) and ESR1-1Estra-1,3 (- 11.05 kcal/mol). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations confirmed the stability of these complexes with RMSD values below 2.5 A and minimal residue fluctuations. WaterSwap free energy calculations yielded highly favorable binding energies (- 34 to - 37 kcal/mol), further validating stable ligand-protein interactions. ADMET predictions indicated acceptable pharmacokinetic properties and low predicted toxicity for most candidates. Collectively, this integrative AI framework efficiently explores peptide chemical space, enabling the rapid identification of peptide-based and peptidomimetic inhibitors with strong binding affinity and stability. The findings highlight the potential of AI-assisted peptide design as a scalable and cost-effective strategy for developing next-generation therapeutics against endometrial cancer.
abstract_zh: 人工智能（AI）与分子建模的整合为加速治疗发现提供了新机遇。在本研究中，我们开发了一种AI驱动的生成流水线，结合深度强化学习（DRL）、生成对抗网络（GANs）和变分自编码器（VAEs），以设计靶向子宫内膜癌（EC）相关主要蛋白（包括AKT1、ESR1、Connexin-43和CTNNB1）的新型肽类分子。从超过14,200个生成结构中，约2313个肽符合药物相似性和结构标准，并通过深度学习增强的对接进行筛选。排名靠前的肽，如Gitoxoside（-11.53 kcal/mol）和9-Fluoro-11（-11.38 kcal/mol），与AKT1的结合强度优于参考抑制剂Capivasertib（-8.50 kcal/mol）。类似的高亲和力相互作用也见于CTNNB1-SCHEMBL（-12.33 kcal/mol）和ESR1-1Estra-1,3（-11.05 kcal/mol）。分子动力学（MD）模拟确认了这些复合物的稳定性，RMSD值低于2.5 Å，且残基波动最小。WaterSwap自由能计算产生了非常有利的结合能（-34至-37 kcal/mol），进一步验证了稳定的配体-蛋白相互作用。ADMET预测表明，大多数候选物具有可接受的药代动力学特性和低预测毒性。总体而言，这一集成AI框架高效探索了肽化学空间，能够快速识别具有强结合亲和力和稳定性的基于肽及肽模拟物抑制剂。这些发现凸显了AI辅助肽设计作为开发下一代子宫内膜癌治疗策略的可扩展且成本效益高的方法的潜力。
